_: Merging two copies of the ledger, with nothing arbitrating. Records are written [id, updated, live|dead, name]; 'want' is the id->name the merge must produce, or DEAD for a tombstone. Every case is run BOTH ways round (a+b and b+a) by the replay, because order-independence is the property that makes a serverless sync work at all.

cases._: A tie is an echo of our own write coming back. Keeping the incumbent is what makes that a no-op; preferring the incoming copy would let two devices trade one record for ever.
cases.name: a tie keeps what was already there
a delete travels as a tombstone and beats an older edit

cases._: The row was deleted on one device and then edited on another, later. Later wins, so it comes back. That is the same rule, not an exception to it.
cases.name: an edit newer than the tombstone resurrects the row
a tombstone for a row the other side never had is still kept
many records merge independently of one another

_properties: Checked by the replay over every case above rather than written out as vectors, because they are statements about the FUNCTION and not about any one input: merging is idempotent (a+a = a), associative ((a+b)+c = a+(b+c)), and commutative except where two records tie exactly, which is the one case no rule can separate.
_migration: A v1 store has no merge clock. Each record's `updated` is seeded from its `created` — the last moment we know it was written — so any later edit on any device outranks it. Seeding from 'now' would make every device claim every old row was the newest.
